- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes or volatility.
- Forecasts often peak too early or too high, then gradually decline — suggesting overshoot followed by mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window, particularly when true values show a downward trend.
- Forecast bias is often upward, especially when historical mean is below 70–75; model consistently forecasts higher than true mean.
- Lagged corrections: model reacts too slowly to recent price drops; true values often dip below forecast before model adjusts.
- When true outcome shows a sharp decline after a peak, model fails to anticipate the drop, leading to overestimation in subsequent days.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to adjust to new trends quickly, especially when true values deviate from prior 7–10 day patterns.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days of the 30-day window, then gradually converge — suggesting model overweights recent volatility.
